results.title: Bayesian Optimization with Active Constraint Learning for ...
results.content: Active learning (AL) and Bayesian Optimization (BayesOpt) are two subfields of machine learning-based sequential design methods that iteratively query the most informative unlabeled data via acquisition function to refine the surrogate model of advanced manufacturing processes with a limited amount of data (Bukkapatnam, Citation2023). Refining the feasible boundary via standard active learning methods like uncertainty-based sampling (Khatamsaz *et al*., Citation2023, Citation2022), as shown in , would trigger numerous additional human annotation processes to estimate the feasible design space that incorporates optimal design correctly. The major contribution of this study lies in that we fused AL and BayesOpt sampling in a unified framework that works collaboratively in an iterative process (i) to learn the feasibility of the experimental design and (ii) to optimize the target quality of process with minimal experiments efforts.
